page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The host provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio (2.0 GB per core). Per-core cache specs include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 variants (f, vnni, bf16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI for accelerated vector arithmetic and cryptographic tasks. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng tests and high text processing capabilities in Geekbench evaluation. Multi-threaded processing and general compute scores, such as PassMark CPU and software compilation, sit within the middle average band. However, memory bandwidth testing reveals performance bottlenecks: while small cached memory transfers perform adequately, large block uncached read speeds fall in the bottom 25% percentile, and large block uncached write bandwidth drops into the bottom 10%. Consequently, memory-bound workloads or larger LLM prompt processing (such as medium 7B parameter models) show degraded throughput.

The lower memory-to-vCPU allocation reduces resource overhead costs for processing tasks that do not demand extensive RAM capacity. The c3d-highcpu-8 offers balanced core density for compute-bound tasks where instruction-level efficiency and single-threaded performance matter most. It is well suited for web serving, microservices, light build and compilation jobs, text parsing, and general algorithmic tasks that stay well within the available 16 GB RAM footprint without saturating uncached system memory bandwidth.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a strict 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Hardware capabilities feature AVX-512 extensions, SHA_NI, and VAES vector cryptography, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-core execution speed and text processing, while overall multi-core performance, web serving throughput, and database operations rank in the average tier. Uncached memory bandwidth represents a key limitation, testing in the lower percentiles for large data transfers. Lacking local storage and GPUs, c3d-highcpu-8 provides cost-efficient CPU resource density tailored for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, text parsing, and microservices that do not rely on high memory capacity.
